messages.subject: REVERSE SIGMOIDAL EFFECT
parts:
Dear INLA users, 

I am trying to incorporate a reverse sigmoidal effect to a model. However I have some questions about that:
  • The first one is regard to the default priors for this effect, in particular, for beta. I have seen in the explanation about this effect that, default priors for the hyperparameters are: beta= theta1 \sim N(mean=1, sd=10), log(a)=theta2 \sim logGamma(3,1) and log(k)=theta3 \sim logGamma(10,10). Then, my question is: is there any way to specify these hyperpriors using pc-priors? 
  • The second one is about the tiny noise of this effect. As you explain, it is used to implement the effect as a latent model, my question is, what is the default value for the precision of this effect? And, is there any recomended way to choose the value for this precision?  
Thank a lot!

Best wishes,

Joaquín.

> 
> I am trying to incorporate a reverse sigmoidal effect to a model.
> However I have some questions about that:
> The first one is regard to the default priors for this effect, in
> particular, for beta. I have seen in the explanation about this
> effect that, default priors for the hyperparameters are:
> beta= theta1 \sim N(mean=1, sd=10), log(a)=theta2 \sim logGamma(3,1)
> and log(k)=theta3 \sim logGamma(10,10). Then, my question is: is
> there any way to specify these hyperpriors using pc-priors?

we have not computed the pc-priors in these cases, but if someone has,
it would be great to know.

> The second one is about the tiny noise of this effect. As you
> explain, it is used to implement the effect as a latent model, my
> question is, what is the default value for the precision of this
> effect? And, is there any recomended way to choose the value for this
> precision?

the default value is

  precision = 1.0e9,

which translate into a stdev of 3E-5

it should not make a difference if this is set small enough. if its to
small then the joint matrix could be numerical singular... 

H



--
Håvard Rue
